model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between coverage and the number of completions (k) for four different Llama model configurations: Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. The x-axis, labeled “Number of completions (k),” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 2⁰ (1) to 2⁸ (256), with tick marks at each power of two. The y-axis, labeled “Coverage,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0.4 to 0.8, with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The Llama-3B line (solid blue with circular markers) starts at approximately 0.42 when k=1 and rises steadily to about 0.87 at k=256. The Llama-3B + FT line (dashed green with triangular markers) begins slightly lower at ~0.41, then increases more steeply, reaching ~0.86 at k=256. The Llama-1B line (solid light blue with square markers) starts at ~0.30 and climbs to ~0.80. The Llama-1B + FT line (dashed light green with diamond markers) begins at ~0.31 and rises to ~0.81. All lines show a consistent upward trend, indicating that coverage improves as the number of completions increases, with Llama-3B and Llama-3B + FT achieving higher coverage across the range compared to their 1B counterparts.
